Gospel authored courtyard props — Poly Haven CC0 source derivations
Revision: gospel-authored-2026-10-27

Source/license/index: Tools/Art/GospelAuthored/source-manifest.json
License: https://polyhaven.com/license — CC0 1.0 Universal.
Original downloaded files and their MD5/SHA verification remain in
Tools/Art/GospelAuthored/Source and the parent source manifest, without duplicates.

Searsia Lucida: https://polyhaven.com/a/searsia_lucida
James Ray Cock (modeling), Jenelle van Heerden (photography).
Actual authored A/B plants become render LODs; authored F is a smaller shrub.
This South African source plant is an artistic courtyard shade tree, not an
identified olive or a reconstruction of vegetation in the historical Temple.

Stone Fire Pit: https://polyhaven.com/a/stone_fire_pit
Sebastian Platen. The irregular stone ring is normalized and made shallower as
an artistic water basin. A separate quiet-water disc covers its inner floor;
no fire, charred timber, Christian statue or historical facility claim is added.

Ceramic Pot: https://polyhaven.com/a/ceramic_pot
Aron Łyczek. Authored handled/lidded ceramic scan, normalized for height.

Planter Pot Clay: https://polyhaven.com/a/planter_pot_clay
Amal Kumar. Authored weathered terracotta scan, normalized for height.

Original 1K albedo and OpenGL normal maps are copied unchanged. Tree RGB and the
separate original alpha atlas are packed through Blender into one RGBA PNG;
decoded RGB and alpha are independently verified identical to the sources.
No photograph is painted or retouched. Retained foliage islands keep original
UVs; branch geometry is decimated for LODs. ARM maps remain in the source index
but are not incorrectly assigned as whole-map occlusion textures.

Actual derived FBX re-import checks and an asset-studio render are recorded in
derivation-manifest.json. These are not Unity/browser execution, archaeological
reconstruction, physical-device performance tests, or user aesthetic approval.
